To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

three new cyclic peroxylactone derivatives, plakortolide H (1), plakortolde I (2), the new 1,3-dioxolane andavadoic (3), and the known N(1)-methyladenosine (4), were isolated from the sponge Plakorits aff simplex.
the new cyclic peroxide andadavadoic acid, isolated from Plakortis, showed cytotoxicity against 13 human tumor cell lines.

the MeOH-Ethyl Acetate (1:1, v/v) extract of the marine sponge Placortis aff simplex collected in Madagascar, has shown cytotoxic activities against a series of human cancer cell lines, and the isolation of four compounds, including one new andavadoic Acid (3) and three new plakortolide H (1), I (2) and N(3)-Methyladenine (3).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the chemical and biological investigation of a new collection of the sponge Pl. aff simplex.
the chemical and biological study of marine organisms, especially sponges, with the aim of discovering new biologically active compounds.
the isolation and characterization of bioactive metabolites from marine organisms, with the aim to discover new drugs for the treatment of cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cytotoxic activity of the sponge is due to the presence of the new peroxylactone 3.
the new compounds 1-3, as well as the known compound 4, have a promising antitumor potential.
the cytotoxicity of andavadoic acids is mainly based on the presence of the peroxide group.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cytotoxic activity of Plakortis species is not due to one compound, but rather a mixture of compounds, and this mixture of compounds is responsible for the cytotoxic activity.
1-3 and 5 are cytotoxic compounds with different mechanisms of action, and 4 has been isolated for the first time in nature.

the new peroxides are the first examples of cyclic peroxides isolated from the marine sponge P. aff simplex and that they represent the first report of cyclic peroxylactone peroxides isolated in the genus Plakortis.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the cytotoxicity of the MeOH-Ethyl acetate extract of P. aff simplex is due to a mixture of the three compounds, plakortolide H (1), plakortololide I (2) and andavadoic Acid (3), with plakortoloides H and I contributing the most.
andavadoic (3) acid is a potent cytotoxic agent with a broad spectrum of activity.
the new 1,3-dioxolane peroxylate (3) isolated from the sponge Plakoritis aff simplex, collected off the coast of Madagascar, is the most cytotoxic compound isolated from the genus Plakortis to date.
